",\n maps = {\n") for key, mp in pairs (MAPS) do f:write (string.format (" [%q] = { edges = {\n", key)) for from, t in pairs (mp.edges) do local parts = {} for d, to in pairs (t) do parts[#parts + 1] = string.format ("[%q]=%d", d, to) end f:write (string.format (" [%d]={%s},\n", from, table.concat (parts, ","))) end f:write (" }, exits = {\n") for from, t in pairs (mp.exits) do local parts = {} for d in pairs (t) do parts[#parts + 1] = string.format ("[%q]=true", d) end f:write (string.format (" [%d]={%s},\n", from, table.concat (parts, ","))) end f:write (" } },\n") end f:write (" },\n") -- the long-term "which exits stay put" record f:write (" learned = {\n") for key, rooms in pairs (learned) do f:write (string.format (" [%q] = {\n", key)) for from, ds in pairs (rooms) do local parts = {} for d, e in pairs (ds) do parts[#parts + 1] = string.format ("[%q]={%d,%d,%d}", d, e.to, e.n, e.bad) end if #parts > 0 then f:write (string.format (" [%d]={%s},\n", from, table.concat (parts, ","))) end end f:write (" },\n") end f:write (" },\n") f:write ("}\n") f:close () end
local function load_map () local f = io.open (DATA_FILE, "r") if not f then return end local body = f:read ("*a") f:close () local chunk = loadstring (body or "") if not chunk then return end local ok, t = pcall (chunk) if not ok or type (t) ~= "table" then return end move_wait = tonumber (t.wait) or move_wait -- Saved as `slow` since 3.0, because the default flipped. A file -- written by an older build has neither key, and no key means express - -- which is what everyone should now get without having to ask. express = not (t.slow and true or false) learned = {} for key, rooms in pairs (t.learned or {}) do learned[key] = {} for from, ds in pairs (rooms) do learned[key][from] = {} for d, v in pairs (ds) do learned[key][from][d] = { to = v[1], n = v[2], bad = v[3] } end end end area_express = {} for k, v in pairs (t.area_express or {}) do area_express[k] = v and true or false end no_auto = {} for k, v in pairs (t.no_auto or {}) do if v then no_auto[k] = true end end for key, mp in pairs (t.maps or {}) do if MAPS[key] then MAPS[key].edges = mp.edges or {} MAPS[key].exits = mp.exits or {} end end end
local function known_links () local n = 0 for _, t in pairs (edges) do for _, to in pairs (t) do if to > 0 then n = n + 1 end end end return n end
local function absorb_room () local ri = gmcp ("room.info") if type (ri) ~= "table" then return end local num = tonumber (ri.num) if not num then return end cur = num if not A or not NAME[num] then return end visited[num] = true local e = {} if type (ri.exits) == "table" then for d, to in pairs (ri.exits) do e[d] = true -- Outside a maze the MUD tells us where each exit GOES, not just -- that it exists ("Inside a maze, room ids are not shown"). That -- is a link for free, with no move spent finding it. local v = tonumber (to) if v and v > 0 and NAME[v] and not is_leaf (num, d) and not (A.sections and A.sections[num] and A.sections[v] and A.sections[num] ~= A.sections[v]) then edges[num] = edges[num] or {} edges[num][d] = v end end end if next (e) == nil then for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do e[d] = true end end exits[num] = e end
-- =========================================================== -- Run state -- ===========================================================
local running = false local phase = nil -- "travel" | "sweep" | "goto" local target = nil -- vnum, for a goto local want = nil -- normalised mob name, for a hunt local want_desc = nil -- phrase to look for in the room listing local want_show = nil -- how to print it local pending = nil -- { from = vnum, dir = d } local queued = {} -- directions still to walk (a scan beeline) local gen = 0 local steps = 0 -- Every move gets its own id, and its stall timer carries it. Without -- that, the timer armed for one move fires while the NEXT one is in -- flight and blames it: it marks a perfectly good exit as a dead wall and -- starts a resync. Walking room to room that mostly went unnoticed; -- waiting on a click between rooms made it fatal. local move_id = 0 local scanning = false
local here_mobs = {} -- roomchars for the room we are standing in local rc_open = false local scan_room = nil -- room the outstanding scan was asked from local arrival = 0 -- bumped on every arrival, guards the decision local decided = true -- has this arrival been acted on yet? local rc_blocks = 0 -- how many room listings we have actually seen local rooms_hit = 0 -- how many rooms we have walked into local noscan_mode = false -- every Nenukon mob scans, so this stays false local want_range = nil -- the rooms this mob is actually seen in local wide = false -- 'all <mob>' ignores the room range local leaving = nil -- the way out we are walking to local stepping_back = false -- undoing a move that left the area local recovers = 0 -- times we have climbed back in this run local journey = nil -- a second leg to run once we cross over local awaiting_leg = false -- crossed over, waiting to land local menu_on_arrival = false -- walked in from outside; show the list local want_levels = nil -- ordered sections to search, most likely first local level_i = 1 -- which of them we are on local crossing = nil local xover = nil -- the crossing under way, and the hunt it serves local cross_from = nil -- the section we left local awaiting_cross = false local where_wait = false local where_settling = false -- an answer has landed, brief wait for more
local where_room = nil -- the room a 'where' pinned, if any local out_walk = false -- this walk is "get me out", so ANY way out will do local reopened = false -- crossed-off exits given a second chance local widened = false -- a mob's usual rooms gave out, now sweeping wider local wipes = 0 -- maps thrown away this run because they went stale local rc_seen = false -- a {roomchars} block arrived for THIS room local rc_waited = false -- and we have already given it one extra second local rc_warned = false -- only nag about a missing room listing once -- How long to wait for a move to be answered before treating that exit as -- dead. Generous by default: a spurious timeout is far more damaging than -- a slow one, because the exit gets written off. 'nenukon wait <secs>'.
local resyncing = false -- waiting on a GMCP room request after a stall local stalls = 0 -- moves in a row that went unanswered local dump_here = false -- 'nenukon here' waiting on a room listing local debug_on = false -- 'nenukon debug': show what the plugin is seeing local scan_hits = {} -- { dir = "n", dist = 2, name = "the roper" } local scan_dir, scan_dist = nil, nil
local sightings = {} -- everything seen this sweep: mob -> vnum
local MAXSTEPS = 600
-- How many times to go round a mob's rooms before calling it absent. These -- mobs move while we are walking, so they can slip into a room already -- ticked off this lap - one or two passes proves very little. local LAP_LIMIT = 4
local function stop (msg, bad) running = false resyncing = false stepping_back = false if where_wait then where_wait = false EnableTriggerGroup ("mm_where", false) end -- Only a real abort forgets a crossing. begin() calls stop () with no -- message to tidy up before a fresh run, and the walk to a portal is -- itself a begin (), so wiping it there loses the hunt every time. if msg then xover, crossing, awaiting_cross = nil, nil, false end step_waiting, step_go, step_action = false, false, nil out_walk = false phase = nil pending = nil target = nil want = nil queued = {} scanning = false gen = gen + 1 EnableTriggerGroup ("mm_scan", false) save_map () if msg then if bad then warn (msg) else note (msg) end end end
-- =========================================================== -- Pathfinding over learned links -- ===========================================================
local function bfs (from, goalfn) if goalfn (from) then return {} end local seen, back = { [from] = true }, {} local q, head = { from }, 1 while head <= #q do local r = q[head] head = head + 1 local t = edges[r] if t then for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do local to = t[d] if to and to > 0 and not seen[to] then seen[to] = true back[to] = { r, d } if goalfn (to) then local path, n = {}, to while n ~= from do local p = back[n] table.insert (path, 1, p[2]) n = p[1] end return path end q[#q + 1] = to end end end end return nil end
-- Only ever explore inside the mob's own range. Rooms outside it are -- still walked through, but their unknown exits are left alone. local function untried (r) local ex = exits[r] if not ex then return nil end local kn = edges[r] -- A level crossing that happens to be a plain direction (Infamy's way -- down from 26669) must not be wandered into while exploring, or the -- sweep drops a level without meaning to and carries on down there. -- Nothing on another level is ours to explore. Some of these rooms -- are joined by links the mapper already knows, so without this the -- search wanders off the level it is meant to be sweeping. if want_levels and A and A.sections and A.sections[r] and A.sections[r] ~= want_levels[level_i] then return nil end local off if A and A.sections and A.bridges then local b = A.bridges[A.sections[r]] if b and b.room == r then off = {} for _, c in ipairs (b.cmds or {}) do off[c] = true end for _, c in ipairs (b.alts or {}) do off[c] = true end end end local hint = hinted[r] for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do -- a hinted link still counts as untried: we have not walked it if ex[d] and not (off and off[d]) and (not (kn and kn[d]) or (hint and hint[d])) then return d end end return nil end
-- =========================================================== -- Walking -- ===========================================================
local move, advance, after_arrival
-- What this walk is for, so the Next line can say so. local function step_subject () if xover and xover.show then return xover.show end if want_show then return want_show end if leaving then return leaving.label or roomname (leaving.room) end if target then return roomname (target) end return nil end
-- The click that walks one more room. We are ready straight away - type -- mmg and it goes - but the LINE waits a fifth of a second, because GMCP lands -- before the room description does and printing now would put it above -- the description, where it just scrolls away. local function offer_step (kind, dir) step_waiting = true step_action = kind step_dir = dir step_room = cur step_token = step_token + 1 DoAfterSpecial (0.2, "mm_step_link (" .. step_token .. ")", 12) end
function mm_step_link (tok) if tok ~= step_token or not step_waiting then return end flush_notes_now () local what = step_subject () local hunting = want_show or (xover and xover.show) local lead = hunting and " - still looking for " or " - on the way to " ColourTell (CLR_TAG, "", "[", CLR_NAME, "", "MazeMobber", CLR_TAG, "", "] ") Hyperlink ("mmg", "NEXT", "Walk one more room", CLR_HI, "black", 0, 1) ColourTell (CLR_MSG, "", " or ", CLR_HI, "", "MMG", CLR_MSG, "", " to continue") if what then ColourNote (CLR_MSG, "", lead, CLR_HI, "", what) else ColourNote (CLR_TAG, "", "") end end
function move (dir) -- One room at a time - except walking OUT. Stepping is a failsafe for -- searching rooms you have not seen; leaving is a known route to a -- known room, and clicking through it while something chews on you is -- no kind of safety. A fight still stops it. if not step_go and not is_express () then offer_step ("move", dir) return end step_go = false
steps = steps + 1 if steps > MAXSTEPS then stop ("Gave up after " .. MAXSTEPS .. " moves.", true) return end pending = { from = cur, dir = dir } move_id = move_id + 1 -- Some exits are behind a door that has to be opened first (Sahuagin's -- four trapdoors down into the maze). Sending "open" at a door that is -- already open just says so, so there is nothing to track or undo. local door = A and A.doors and A.doors[cur] and A.doors[cur][dir] if door then for _, c in ipairs (door) do SendNoEcho (c) end end -- SendNoEcho, not Send. Echoing the command writes to the output -- window, and a line the MUD sends straight afterwards can no longer be -- omitted by anything - which is why Aardwolf's {rdesc} marker leaked -- on every arrival while {/rdesc}, arriving mid-description, did not. -- Walking silently also spares you a screen of n/e/s/w echoes. SendNoEcho (dir) DoAfterSpecial (move_wait, "mm_timeout (" .. gen .. "," .. move_id .. ")", 12) end
local function start_scan () scan_hits = {} scan_dir, scan_dist = nil, nil scanning = true scan_room = cur -- so late output from a room we have left is dropped EnableTriggerGroup ("mm_scan", true) SendNoEcho ("scan") end
-- One decision per arrival. Whichever comes first - the scan finishing -- or this fallback - acts, and the other is ignored. local function schedule_decision (seconds) arrival = arrival + 1 decided = false DoAfterSpecial (seconds, "mm_decide (" .. gen .. "," .. arrival .. ")", 12) end
-- Nearest room we have not stood in yet. With a range in force this -- only ever aims at rooms the mob actually uses. -- Every room on one level of an area. local function rooms_of (section) local t = {} if not (A and A.sections) then return t end for v, sec in pairs (A.sections) do if sec == section then t[v] = true end end return t end
-- Room names that belong to exactly one room, so a 'where' hit on one -- pins the room - and with it the level - outright. local UNIQUE = {} for _, a in ipairs (AREAS) do local count, first = {}, {} for v, nm in pairs (a.roomname) do count[nm] = (count[nm] or 0) + 1 first[nm] = first[nm] or v end UNIQUE[a.key] = {} for nm, c in pairs (count) do if c == 1 then UNIQUE[a.key][nm:lower ()] = first[nm] end end end
-- Use the way out we walked to: some need a command, some you just -- walk up from yourself. -- Exits we crossed off - dead ends, and ways out of the area - are only -- ever a belief about how the maze was arranged at the time. A repop can -- move them, and a door that was shut can be open. Rather than declare -- somewhere unreachable while still holding those, rub them out and have -- another go: being wrong here costs a few moves, and being stubborn -- costs the whole search. local function reopen_crossed () local n = 0 for from, t in pairs (edges) do for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do if t[d] == 0 or t[d] == -1 then t[d] = nil; n = n + 1 end end end return n end
-- Is this way out one of the area's own ways out? The entries come -- straight from A.outs, so identity is enough. local function is_way_out (o) if not (A and A.outs) then return false end for _, e in ipairs (A.outs) do if e == o then return true end end return false end
-- Said once you have got where you were going, in the areas you cannot -- just recall out of. A plain note so it queues with everything else and -- lands under the room description in the right order. local function remind_out () if not (A and A.outs and #A.outs > 0) then return end note ("Done here? @x048mmout@w or @x048mmo@w walks you back out of " .. A.label .. ".") end
local function take_exit () local o = leaving if not o then return end -- Only a crossing the PLUGIN chose gets its own click. When you picked -- "Dive Room" or typed mmo, arriving and doing the thing is the whole -- request - making you click again to send "surface" while standing in -- the room just looks broken. A level crossing mid-hunt is different: -- that is the plugin deciding to move you somewhere new. if o.cmds and xover and not step_go then offer_step ("exit") return end leaving = nil step_go = false if o.cmds then note ("At @x048" .. (o.label or roomname (o.room)) .. "@w - sending @x048" .. table.concat (o.cmds, "@w, @x048") .. "@w.") -- ...unless this IS the way out, in which case you are leaving if not is_way_out (o) then remind_out () end -- Armed before sending, not after: the room change can land before -- Send even returns. if journey then awaiting_leg = true end if xover then awaiting_cross = true end for _, c in ipairs (o.cmds) do SendNoEcho (c) end elseif is_way_out (o) then -- A way OUT with no command of its own: the walk is done but you are -- still inside, so say what is left to do. note ("At @x048" .. (o.label or roomname (o.room)) .. "@w (@x048" .. o.room .. "@w). I do not know the command that leaves from here - " .. o.how .. " yourself and you are clear.") else -- A room you asked to be walked to. Getting there IS the whole job - -- there is nothing left to send. This used to fall through to the -- message above and tell you it did not know the command that leaves -- from here, which reads as a failure at the exact moment it -- succeeded. An area with no A.outs leaves under its own steam, so -- remind_out () stays quiet there too. note ("Arrived: @x048" .. (o.label or roomname (o.room)) .. "@w (@x048" .. o.room .. "@w)") remind_out () end end
-- One room, whether it was mmg, a click on NEXT, or another mmout. local function step_once () local st = gmcp ("char.status") if type (st) == "table" and tonumber (st.state) == 8 then warn ("You are in combat - finish the fight first.") return true end if not step_waiting then return false end step_waiting = false local what, dir = step_action, step_dir step_action, step_dir = nil, nil
-- Arriving at the room a way out is in ends the walk to it, so running -- is already false by then; only `leaving` says what is left to do. if what == "exit" and leaving then step_go = true take_exit () step_go = false return true end if not running then return false end step_go = true if dir then move (dir) else advance () end step_go = false return true end
-- Move to the level we want to be searching. The crossings form a ring -- (1 to 2 to 3 and back to 1), so taking the next one repeatedly reaches -- any level from any other; we re-check after each hop rather than -- planning the whole route up front. local function cross_step () if not (A and A.sections and want_levels) then return false end local here, target = A.sections[cur], want_levels[level_i] if not target or here == target then return false end
local b = A.bridges and A.bridges[here] if not b then stop ("I know no way off " .. tostring (here) .. " in " .. A.label .. " - stopped.", true) return true end
-- Walking to the portal is a goto, and starting one wipes the hunt. -- So the hunt travels with the crossing and is put back on the far -- side, which works whether the move lands now or in a second. -- If the way across is a plain direction it can move about (Infamy's -- way down from 26669 was up last repop and may not be next), so the -- room's other exits are the fallbacks, worked out fresh each time -- rather than crossed off a shared list for good. local alts = {} local one = b.cmds and #b.cmds == 1 and b.cmds[1] local is_dir = false for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do if d == one then is_dir = true break end end if is_dir then for _, d in ipairs (DIRS) do if d ~= one and exits[b.room] and exits[b.room][d] then alts[#alts + 1] = d end end end for _, d in ipairs (b.alts or {}) do alts[#alts + 1] = d end xover = { b = b, from = here, alts = alts, levels = want_levels, li = level_i, range = want_range, want = want, show = want_show, desc = want_desc, noscan = noscan_mode } crossing, cross_from = b, here leaving = b note ("Heading for @x048" .. target .. "@w via @x048" .. (b.label or b.how) .. "@w.") if cur == b.room then take_exit () else begin ("goto", b.room, nil, false) end return true end
-- Nearest room we have not stood in yet. With a range in force this only -- aims at rooms the mob actually uses. Otherwise rooms an area marks as -- "late" are left until last - the Gauntlet's BATTLE ROOM is a dead end -- with the Deep Dragon in it, so a sweep has no business going in early. local function path_to_unvisited () if want_range then return bfs (cur, function (v) return want_range[v] and not visited[v] end) end local late = A.late local p = bfs (cur, function (v) return not visited[v] and not late[v] end) if p and p[1] then return p end for tier = 1, 9 do p = bfs (cur, function (v) return not visited[v] and late[v] == tier end) if p and p[1] then return p end end return nil end
-- Arrived somewhere: for a scannable mob, scan and decide when it comes -- back. For the noscan pair scanning is pointless - they never appear in -- it - so we send nothing and decide off the room's own character list, -- with a timer to cover rooms that list nobody at all. local function begin_room () rooms_hit = rooms_hit + 1 -- Areas that list rooms rather than mobs have nothing scan could tell -- us, so they never scan. if noscan_mode or #MOBS == 0 then -- No wait at all. We cannot tell "nobody here" from "the listing has -- not arrived yet" - an empty room sends no {roomchars} block to -- trigger on - but it does not matter, because nothing moves without -- a click. So offer the next step immediately; if a listing turns up -- afterwards, mm_rc_end checks it for the mob BEFORE it looks at -- whether we already decided, and we are still standing in the room, -- so the find still happens. Finding it clears step_waiting, which -- stops the delayed link from printing at all. schedule_decision (0.1) else start_scan () schedule_decision (8) end end
-- Pick the next direction: finish a beeline, else head for the target -- room, else take an exit we have never tried, else walk to the nearest -- room that still has one. -- Is there still a room the mob uses that we have not stood in? local function range_left () if not want_range then return true end for v in pairs (want_range) do if not visited[v] then return true end end return false end
function advance () if #queued > 0 then move (table.remove (queued, 1)) return end
-- Walking out is not walking to one particular room: any of the area's -- ways out will do. Nenukon has two, and committing to the first one -- meant strolling through the other and carrying on - 67 clicks where -- the second was reached on the 17th. if phase == "goto" and out_walk then local ways = here_list (A.outs) local standing for _, o in ipairs (ways) do if o.room == cur then standing = o end end if standing then leaving, target = standing, cur else local best, pick for _, o in ipairs (ways) do local p = bfs (cur, function (x) return x == o.room end) if p and (not best or #p < best) then best, pick = #p, o end end if pick and pick.room ~= target then leaving, target = pick, pick.room note ("@x048" .. (pick.label or roomname (pick.room)) .. "@w is the nearer way out now - heading there instead.") end end end
if phase == "goto" then if cur == target then if leaving and leaving.room == cur then stop () take_exit () return end leaving = nil if menu_on_arrival then menu_on_arrival = false stop () menu () return end stop ("Arrived: @x048" .. (NAME[cur] or cur) .. "@w (@x048" .. cur .. "@w)") remind_out () return end local path = bfs (cur, function (v) return v == target end) if path and path[1] then move (path[1]) return end end
-- A hunt goes to the mob's own rooms first; walking the rest of the -- area is only ever a means of reaching them. if phase ~= "goto" then local unseen = path_to_unvisited () if unseen and unseen[1] then move (unseen[1]) return end end
-- Explore, but for a hunt only while a room the mob uses is still out -- of reach over the links we know. if phase == "goto" or range_left () then local d = untried (cur) if d then move (d) return end -- Nearest room that still has an untried exit. Weighting this by how -- MANY untried exits a room has was tried and measured worse: the walk -- discovers nothing, so distance is what actually costs. local path = bfs (cur, function (v) return untried (v) ~= nil end) if path and path[1] then move (path[1]) return end end
if phase == "goto" then if not reopened then local n = reopen_crossed () if n > 0 then reopened = true note ("Every way I know is walked and no sign of it - re-trying " .. "the @x048" .. n .. "@w exits I had crossed off.") return advance () end end -- "Explored everything I can reach" is only ever true of the map we -- happen to be holding, and in a maze that reshuffles that map is -- exactly what goes stale - the room IS reachable, just not by the -- links we wrote down. Throwing the map away and walking on is what -- "<area> reset" does by hand, so do it automatically rather than -- stopping and asking. MAXSTEPS is the real backstop: this cannot -- run forever, it just stops guessing that it is finished. -- Capped, because if a wipe leaves nothing to try we would come -- straight back here and recurse. Three is plenty: each one is a -- fresh sweep of the whole area, and MAXSTEPS bounds the walking. if wipes >= 3 then stop ("Wiped the map and swept " .. wipes .. " times over and still " .. "no sign of it. Something is wrong - walk out and back in.", true) return end wipes = wipes + 1 edges, exits = {}, {} seed () visited, laps = {}, 0 reopened = false note ("Walked everything the map knew and it was not there - the maze " .. "has moved. Forgetting it and carrying on" .. ((wipes > 1) and (" (" .. wipes .. ")") or "") .. ".") return advance () end
-- About to declare failure of some kind, and this room has not sent its -- character list yet. Deciding now is how a mob standing right in -- front of us gets missed: the listing lands a moment later, but the -- hunt is already over so nothing looks at it. Walking on is safe to -- do instantly; giving up is worth one more second. if noscan_mode and not rc_seen and not rc_waited then rc_waited = true schedule_decision (1) return end
-- If we never even got to one of the mob's rooms, this is not "checked -- and not there" - it is "cannot get there from here". Monuhi's crypt, -- for instance, has no exit the mapper knows about. if want_range then local reached = false for v in pairs (want_range) do if visited[v] then reached = true break end end if not reached and not reopened then local n = reopen_crossed () if n > 0 then reopened = true note ("Cannot get to any room it uses - re-trying the @x048" .. n .. "@w exits I had crossed off.") return advance () end end if not reached and not widened then -- In a maze that reshuffles, "have not reached it" is NOT "cannot -- reach it". The links move, so the only way into a room may be to -- keep walking until one leads there. Knowing where a mob usually -- stands should make the hunt shorter, never make it give up early - -- so drop back to searching everything and carry on. widened = true want_range = want_levels and rooms_of (want_levels[level_i]) or nil -- Clearing visited lets the wider sweep re-check rooms the mob may -- have moved into since. The room we are STANDING in has to go -- straight back in, though: the very next thing this does is ask -- whether any room in range has been reached, and on a freshly -- emptied table the answer was no - so it gave up anyway. visited, laps = {}, 0 visited[cur] = true note ("Not got to where @x048" .. (want_show or "it") .. "@w usually is yet - searching the rest of @x048" .. ((want_levels and want_levels[level_i]) or A.label) .. "@w.") return advance () end if not reached then stop ("I could not reach a single room @x048" .. (want_show or "it") .. "@w uses, starting from @x048" .. (NAME[cur] or cur) .. "@w - there is no route I know of out of here. Walk out and " .. "try again.", true) return end end
-- A full lap done. These mobs wander, so one clean lap is not proof it -- is not here - go round again before giving up. -- This level is done. If the mob is known on another one, cross over -- and keep going rather than giving up. The levels are a ring: going -- round them all counts as one lap, so a mob that moves between them -- gets the same benefit of the doubt as one that moves between rooms. if want_levels and #want_levels > 1 then local was_level = want_levels[level_i] local nxt = level_i + 1 if nxt > #want_levels then nxt = 1 laps = laps + 1 end if laps < LAP_LIMIT then level_i = nxt want_range = RANGE[want] or rooms_of (want_levels[level_i]) visited = {} note ("Not on " .. was_level .. " - trying @x048" .. want_levels[level_i] .. "@w.") if cross_step () then return end return advance () end end
